# Crosswalk coverage at CodeMeta 3.1

<!-- Generated by `codemeta-drift hub coverage examples/mapping-3.1.json --codemeta <checkout>`; edit the curated rows, not this file. -->

How CodeMeta's 3.1 crosswalks map 17 CodeMeta terms in 9 formats, read from the reviewed [mapping export](mapping-export.md). PEP 621 has no CodeMeta crosswalk, so each of its paths is added here. This page shows the pinned tag; the [web page](https://simonvanlierde.com/codemeta-drift/) also checks CodeMeta's main branch each week.

| Mark | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | as-is | CodeMeta's crosswalk cell is the path, used unchanged |
| ✎ | corrected | the crosswalk cell is wrong, ambiguous or prose; a curated row replaces it |
| + | added | the format has the field but the crosswalk has no cell for it; a curated row adds it |
| – | no field | the format has no field for this term |

## Curated cells

### cff-1.2.0

- `author.@id` (corrected): crosswalk cell `person.orcid / identifiers / doi` → `authors[].orcid`. The cell lists person.orcid / identifiers / doi; a person's ORCID is orcid.
- `contributor` (no field): no crosswalk cell → no path. No cell for contributors; CFF 1.2.0 has no contributor list, only authors.
- `contributor.givenName` (no field): crosswalk cell `person.given-names` → no path. No cell for contributors; CFF 1.2.0 has no contributor list, only authors.
- `contributor.familyName` (no field): crosswalk cell `person.family-names` → no path. No cell for contributors; CFF 1.2.0 has no contributor list, only authors.
- `contributor.@id` (no field): crosswalk cell `person.orcid / identifiers / doi` → no path. No cell for contributors; CFF 1.2.0 has no contributor list, only authors.
- `license` (corrected): crosswalk cell `license / license-url` → `license`. The cell lists license / license-url; license-url holds a licence URL, not an SPDX id.
- `identifier` (corrected): crosswalk cell `identifiers / person.orcid / doi` → `doi | identifiers[type=doi].value`. The cell lists identifiers / person.orcid / doi; the software DOI is doi, or the doi entry of identifiers.
- `swhid` (corrected): crosswalk cell `identifiers / person.orcid / doi` → `identifiers[type=swh].value`. The cell lists identifiers / person.orcid / doi; a SWHID is the swh entry of identifiers.

### bibtex

- `version` (added): no crosswalk cell → `version`. No cell; biblatex and biblatex-software keep the version in version.
- `author.givenName` (added): no crosswalk cell → `author`. No cell; BibTeX keeps every author in one author string, names joined by and, each written 'Given Family' or 'Family, Given'.
- `author.familyName` (added): no crosswalk cell → `author`. No cell; BibTeX keeps every author in one author string, names joined by and, each written 'Given Family' or 'Family, Given'.

- `contributor` (no field): no crosswalk cell → no path. No cell; a software entry has no contributor field.

- `identifier` (corrected): crosswalk cell `doi / hal_id` → `doi`. The cell lists doi / hal_id; hal_id is a HAL archive id, the DOI is doi.
- `swhid` (corrected): crosswalk cell `doi / hal_id` → `swhid`. The cell lists doi / hal_id for every identifier; biblatex-software keeps the SWHID in swhid.
- `keywords` (added): no crosswalk cell → `keywords`. No cell; biblatex keeps keywords in keywords, separated by commas.
- `datePublished` (corrected): crosswalk cell `date / (year) / (month)` → `date | year`. The cell lists date / (year) / (month); biblatex writes the release date in date, and classic BibTeX gives only year and month.
